<description>
Several numeric configuration options now reject values that are out of range instead of silently wrapping or inverting. Previously a negative value could disable the intended limit entirely.

  - `-dbbatchsize` and `-dbcrashratio` must be non-negative. A negative `-dbbatchsize` wrapped to a huge value and disabled batch flushing, so a reindex could hold an unbounded batch in memory.
  - `-limitclustersize`, `-limitancestorcount`, `-limitdescendantcount`, `-mempoolexpiry`, `-datacarriersize`, `-maxsendbuffer`, `-maxreceivebuffer`, `-bantime`, `-bytespersigop` and `-maxtipage` must be non-negative.
  - `-limitclustercount` must be between 1 and 64.
  - `-timeout` must be positive. It previously fell back to the default silently, unlike the analogous `-peertimeout`, which already errored.

  Zero remains valid wherever it already meant "disabled": `-dbbatchsize=0`,
  `-limitclustersize=0`, `-datacarriersize=0`, `-mempoolexpiry=0`,
  `-maxtipage=0`, `-bytespersigop=0`, `-maxsendbuffer=0`,
  `-maxreceivebuffer=0` and `-bantime=0`.

- The `-help` output for `-bytespersigop`, `-datacarriersize`, `-dbbatchsize`, `-stopatheight` and `-checkblockindex` now shows the `=<n>` placeholder for their value, matching how they are actually parsed.
</description>

[2026-11-13] c:6862113841 comment by l0rinc (member):
Concept ACK

There are lots of AI findings about these potential misconfigurations, so it would be good to close off as many of them as possible in one go.

A few closely related cases seem worth covering as well:
- `-timeout` values above `INT_MAX` are narrowed before the new positivity check (similar ones were already attempted here and closed).
- Very large `-mempoolexpiry` values can overflow when converted from hours to seconds.
- A negative `-txconfirmtarget` wraps into the wallet's unsigned target and can make fee estimation fall back to `-fallbackfee`.
- Negating an integer option is documented as setting it to `0`, so `-nolimitclustersize` and `-nobantime` are equivalent to the zero values this PR explicitly accepts. `-limitclustersize=0` makes every transaction oversized and prevents normal mempool admission, while `-bantime=0` makes `setban` without an explicit duration create an immediately expired ban.

CI seems to fail because the new test loop binds a `std::string` reference to temporary strings.
[2026-11-13] c:6863371683 comment by sedited (member):
See https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36763

But I think I'm Approach NACK at yet another piecemeal approach to a solution for this. This should be solved by the args handler itself, not with many different bug prone special cases.
[2026-11-13] r:5899222221 review COMMENTED by ryanofsky (member):
Concept ACK 1ab3f148582c21054dfc9323623edcf9768949f6 for parsing improvements here, but I'd recommend against increased use of the DISALLOW_NEGATION flag:

- If your option can't accept zero values, DISALLOW_NEGATION is only a partial fix and may allow zeroes to slip through because you are only guarding against them being set ib a single path. Better to check for valid values one place instead of multiple.
- It creates inconsistent UX where -option=0 and -nooption have different behaviors without a clear reason, when normal behavior is for them to behave the same.

DISALLOW_NEGATION was intended to used rarely and eventually removed (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/22766#issuecomment-944924866) and this PR seems to increase usage by a lot. The other changes here look very good though.
